factual_claims.claim: Performance benefited from the beginning of Estonia’s economic recovery, stronger loan demand and greater investment activity.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Managing Director´s Statement: 'In 2025, many macroeconomic indicators improved, and we entered the post-recession recovery phase... Coop Pank followed a growth strategy, and in line with this, we continued to grow both our customer base and loan portfolio in 2025.'

factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating environment: 'Estonia’s real GDP growth in 2025 was 0.7%, according to the Bank of Estonia... Throughout 2025, the turbulence created by the U.S. government in international trade and the resulting uncertainty had a significant impact on the global economy. Compared to 2024, inflation decreased significantly, allowing central banks to continue lowering interest rates, which led to a continued decline in all major base rates until the summer of 2025.'

candidate_sentences.text: Estonia’s GDP grew 0.7% in 2025, while declining inflation and interest rates supported confidence among businesses and households.

factual_claims.claim: However, the six-month Euribor fell to 2.1% by year-end, contributing to pressure on interest income.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating environment: 'For 2026, global economic growth is forecast at 3.1%, but developed countries are expected to grow by just 1.6%. Throughout 2025, the turbulence created by the U.S. government in international trade and the resulting uncertainty had a significant impact on the global economy. Compared to 2024, inflation decreased significantly, allowing central banks to continue lowering interest rates, which led to a continued decline in all major base rates until the summer of 2025. From summer 2025 until the end of the year, the interest rate environment remained stable... For example, the 6-month Euribor, which is linked to most loans of Estonian companies and mortgage loans to individuals, reached a short-term record of 4.1% in October 2023, but fell to 2.1% by the end of 2025.'

factual_claims.claim: It also signed an EIB Group guarantee agreement enabling up to €249 million of new business lending; the transaction had not become effective and had no impact on 2025 results.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Managing Director´s Statement: 'At the end of the year, Coop Pank entered into a guarantee agreement with the European Investment Bank Group, under which part of the credit risk arising from Coop Pank’s loan portfolio will be transferred to EIB Group, thereby providing capital relief to Coop Pank and enabling the bank to issue up to €249 million in new loans to businesses... The new funding will be directed toward projects in Estonia that promote gender equality and environmental sustainability... This is Coop Pank’s first synthetic securitization transaction, and also the first such transaction in the Baltics based entirely on the loan portfolio of a single country – Estonia... The capital relief accompanying the agreement enables the bank to issue new loans to Estonian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and larger mid-cap companies for projects that support gender equality, economic growth, and environmental sustainability... In 2025, the credit rating agency Moody’s affirmed Coop Pank’s deposit rating at Baa2 with a positive outlook.'

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (profitability metrics), K2 (loan portfolio growth), K3 (deposit growth), K4 (customer base expansion), K6 (funding diversification), K7 (capital ratios), and K10 (dividends). However, it omits the strategic targets outlined in K5, sustainability initiatives in K8, product/service expansions in K9, the EEEF loan drawdown in K11, and the Management Board appointment in K12. While several HIGH-priority items are missing (K5, K11), the summary captures most material information, resulting in a 'Generally yes' assessment.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of business growth with declining profitability. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational issues. Explanations for margin pressure (lower interest rates) and growth drivers (loan demand, economic recovery) are consistent throughout. The progression from profitability metrics to balance sheet changes and external factors forms a clear narrative. While there is a minor arithmetic relationship between segment figures and totals (e.g., loan portfolio components vs. total), the candidate does not claim these are exhaustive additive components of the same total, so this does not constitute a contradiction under the specified evaluation criteria.
